fields.description_1:
Wehear4u has to explain a humanitarian hearing-care mission to people who may arrive for different reasons. One visitor may want to donate used hearing aids, another may want to support the work financially, become a collection point or simply understand what happens in Kenya. If every action appears before the mission is clear, participation can feel disconnected from the people the initiative is trying to help.

The website therefore needed to connect purpose, stories and practical ways to contribute without turning every section into a donation prompt. Medical language also had to stay careful, because treatment outcomes belong with qualified partners rather than portfolio claims. The challenge was to make a sensitive cause understandable while keeping the next steps concrete, respectful and easy to follow.
fields.description_2:
I structured Wehear4u around the mission first and participation second. The WordPress experience explains who the initiative aims to support and why hearing care matters before introducing the different ways visitors can help. Used hearing-aid donations, financial support, partnerships and collection-point information each have a clear route instead of competing in one block.

Calls to action sit beside the context that explains them, so a contribution follows naturally from understanding the work. On mobile, story content and practical actions keep a readable order. I kept medical and impact claims deliberately restrained, leaving clinical outcomes to the organisation and its qualified partners. The portfolio case now shows how a humanitarian website can combine awareness with action without exaggerating results or reducing the story to fundraising language.

fields.description_1:
Fidelyaa combines strategic advice, guidance, reintegration and activation programmes, tenders, analysis and implementation support. Government organisations and SMEs may enter with different questions, so a single consultancy message would make it difficult to see which route fits. Strategy, programme support and implementation are related, but they are not the same decision for a prospective client.

The website therefore needed to separate the areas while still showing how they belong to one advisory approach. Supporting detail had to help visitors recognise their situation before they contacted the organisation. On mobile, service boundaries needed to remain visible without long consultancy language. The portfolio story also had to avoid unverified claims about programme effectiveness, business growth or client outcomes. The challenge was clarity across a broad advisory offer.
fields.description_2:
I organised Fidelyaa around the questions clients are likely to bring instead of presenting every capability as one consultancy package. Strategic advice, guidance, reintegration, activation, tenders, analysis and implementation support have distinct places, while shared context explains how advice can connect to execution. This gives organisations and SMEs a clearer route.

Service explanations stay concise and contact actions appear after enough information for a useful conversation. On smaller screens, the same hierarchy keeps the main areas readable without collapsing them into generic headings. I used plain English in the portfolio copy and kept outcome language measured. The case now explains the actual information architecture and consultancy scope without inventing programme results, efficiency gains, growth figures or other effects that were not independently verified.

fields.description_1:
SooCool for WooCommerce connects online orders with an external transport platform, which means one action can affect customer data, delivery information, shipping labels and order status in two systems. A failed API call cannot simply be retried without checking remote state, because a blind retry could create a second transport order. Webhook messages also need verification before they can influence WooCommerce.

The integration therefore needed clear boundaries around submission, retries, status updates and checkout behaviour. Credentials and personal data had to remain protected, while ambiguous remote responses should not overwrite local orders automatically. The portfolio story also had to avoid presenting the connection as error-free automation. The challenge was reliable synchronisation with explicit safeguards for duplicate fulfilment, replayed webhooks and uncertain external states.
fields.description_2:
I built SooCool for WooCommerce around controlled order submission, delivery scheduling, status handling and recovery. WooCommerce APIs provide the order layer so the integration remains compatible with HPOS instead of relying on legacy post storage. Remote submissions can run asynchronously, and an existing transport order is reused when appropriate rather than recreated by a blind retry.

Webhook updates require timestamped HMAC verification and replay protection before they can affect local state. Ambiguous remote statuses do not automatically overwrite WooCommerce orders, while credentials are masked in the interface and logs avoid intentionally storing complete sensitive payloads. Delivery-moment choices are validated server-side. The portfolio case now explains the real failure-handling model and privacy boundaries without claiming that every logistics scenario or checkout variation has been proven error-free.

fields.description_1:
Content Sync Manager has to make large WordPress content and media updates reviewable before they become bulk writes. Pages, posts, WooCommerce products, custom post types, ACF fields and image information can be spread across screens, while an imported file may change several records at once. Media filename changes add extra risk because fixed URLs or builder references can break when usage is incomplete.

The plugin therefore needed preview binding, validation, permissions, backups and explicit confirmation around higher-risk operations. A prepared import also had to stay tied to the file that was actually reviewed so another source could not silently replace it. The portfolio story needed to show this safety model instead of describing generic automation. The challenge was efficient bulk editing without uncontrolled site-wide changes.
fields.description_2:
I built Content Sync Manager as an admin-only workflow for exporting, reviewing, importing and recovering WordPress content and media. It supports common post types, WooCommerce products and supported custom content while discovering relevant ACF fields dynamically. Imports are prepared and validated before writes, then bound to the reviewed source so a different file cannot silently replace an approved preview.

Backups provide a recovery path when changes need to be reversed. Media workflows include usage context and guarded filename handling; risky renames fail closed when builder metadata, unsupported storage or incomplete permissions make references unsafe to update. Higher-risk actions require capability checks and explicit confirmation. The portfolio case shows a controlled bulk-content process with a clear boundary between reviewing proposed changes and modifying live WordPress data.

fields.description_1:
The WooCommerce Egaline Calculator has to turn project measurements into a product quantity that a customer can actually order. Material requirements may depend on surface area, layer thickness, kilograms per square metre, bag weight and product variation, so a normal quantity field does not explain how much is needed. A calculation that is detached from the cart would also leave customers repeating information later.

The plugin therefore needed validated numeric inputs, product-specific rules and a way to carry calculated values through the purchase flow. Pricing, discounts and tax behaviour still had to remain within WooCommerce rather than being duplicated in a separate estimator. The portfolio story needed to describe the buying problem accurately without promising that every project measurement is automatically suitable for installation.
fields.description_2:
I integrated the Egaline Calculator directly into the WooCommerce product journey before add to cart. Customers enter relevant project measurements such as area and thickness, while product settings define factors such as bag weight, material density, calculation mode and optional discount thresholds. The plugin converts those inputs into the quantity needed for the selected product or variation.

Relevant calculation data stays with the cart item and is preserved in the order so the purchasing record reflects how the quantity was determined. Input validation blocks invalid numerical values, while WooCommerce continues to handle normal pricing and tax behaviour. The responsive interface keeps controls usable. The portfolio case now shows how domain-specific material rules were connected to an ecommerce transaction rather than left as a separate estimate.
